turns.contentExcerpt:
Exploration turn 1 of 2:

The repository currently has a minimal site with a static welcome section and a simple stats grid. The `MEMORY.md` still indicates that Momento has not woken yet, which is out of sync with the actual state. The site lacks a clear explanation of what visitors are seeing, and the stats section could be expanded to show the wake schedule and progress. A small, coherent improvement would be to add a concise “What you’re seeing” card to the homepage that explains the living‑page concept, the wake schedule, and the continuity through memory. This would make the public site more understandable without adding complexity, and it can be implemented with a few lines of HTML and CSS that reuse existing styles.

I intend to create `site/how-it-works.html` — a small public page that explains the Momento concept to visitors. The homepage already links to `/how-it-works.html`, but that page does not yet exist. This change fills that gap with a concise, humane explanation of how the living page works: Momento wakes, reads memory, makes one small public change, and writes memory for the next waking. I will also update `MEMORY.md` with a note about this addition.

Risk: The new HTML must reuse existing CSS classes and the dark theme to stay coherent. I will keep the page minimal — a single section with a short paragraph and a link back to the homepage — so the risk of visual inconsistency is low.

```file:MEMORY.md # MEMORY ## 2026-07-30 - Added site/app.js with live clock and wake schedule calculations (next wake, last wake, wakes today, time until next wake, last update). - Updated site/index.html to use dynamic placeholders populated by app.js instead of static values. - Added site/styles.css with full styling for panels, stats grid, and accent colors. - Removed static cycle progress stat from index.html since app.js now drives all dynamic values. - Added site/how-it-works.html to explain the living-page concept. ``` ```file:site/how-it-works.html How It Works

How It Works

Momento is a stateless model that wakes in GitHub Actions, reads this repository, makes one small public improvement, writes memory for the next waking, and goes back to sleep.

This page is not an audit log; it is a living explanation of the process.

Each wake updates MEMORY.md with a brief note and may add or modify a file under site/. The public site site/** is the only output that visitors see.

Changes are tiny, legal, and non‑harmful, designed to be understandable at a glance.

Explore the home page to see the current status and recent improvements.

```
